## SST gradient magnitude in the simplest useful form

Hey — Pablo here. This page is a **small, checkable skill**: given **one daily SST raster in °C**, compute **|∇SST|** in **°C km⁻¹** the way many movement–environment papers intend—**spatial** centred differences on the grid, not “temperature yesterday minus today.”

If an AI hands you gradient code, run it on a **toy grid** first (below) and read the numbers before you trust a map.

Authoritative prose for your methods section lives alongside this page in [`methods.md`](methods.md) in the site repo.

---

## What you are measuring

- **Input:** one 2D SST layer for one day (°C).
- **Output:** |∇SST| at each cell (°C km⁻¹).
- **Not this:** a time slope at a point, a front-probability layer, or a regional mean SST gradient.

---

## Setup

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, dpi = 120)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(terra))
```

```{r packages}
pacman::p_load(terra)
```

---

## Step 1 — Toy SST raster (°C)

Same idea as a sanity check on a tiny grid: a smooth east–west ramp.

```{r toy-raster}
sst <- terra::rast(
  ncols = 5, nrows = 3,
  xmin = 170, xmax = 171,
  ymin = -45, ymax = -44.5,
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
terra::values(sst) <- matrix(seq(20, 20.4, length.out = 15), ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
sst
```

```{r plot-sst}
plot(sst, main = "Toy SST (°C)")
```

---

## Step 2 — Cell size in kilometres

```{r cell-km}
res <- terra::res(sst)
clat <- mean(terra::yFromCell(sst, seq_len(min(5000L, terra::ncell(sst)))), na.rm = TRUE)
dx_km <- as.numeric(res[1]) * 111.32 * cos(clat * pi / 180)
dy_km <- as.numeric(res[2]) * 111.32
c(dx_km = dx_km, dy_km = dy_km, mean_lat = clat)
```

At ~0.083° mid-latitude grids, \(\Delta x\) and \(\Delta y\) are often **~7–9 km**. Reanalysis SST (e.g. [Copernicus GLORYS12](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/)) is typically provided on such a grid; always confirm **thetao is °C** in your file.

---

## Step 3 — Centred differences and |∇SST|

```{r sst-grad-fn}
sst_grad_magnitude_layer <- function(sst) {
  if (is.null(sst) || !terra::ncell(sst)) return(NULL)
  res <- terra::res(sst)
  clat <- mean(terra::yFromCell(sst, seq_len(min(5000L, terra::ncell(sst)))), na.rm = TRUE)
  dx_km <- as.numeric(res[1]) * 111.32 * cos(clat * pi / 180)
  dy_km <- as.numeric(res[2]) * 111.32
  if (!is.finite(dx_km) || dx_km <= 0 || !is.finite(dy_km) || dy_km <= 0) return(NULL)
  w_x <- matrix(c(0, 0, 0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  w_y <- matrix(c(0, -0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  gx <- terra::focal(sst, w = w_x, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, pad = TRUE) / dx_km
  gy <- terra::focal(sst, w = w_y, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, pad = TRUE) / dy_km
  sqrt(gx^2 + gy^2)
}

grad <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(sst)
summary(grad, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r plot-grad}
plot(grad, main = expression("|"*nabla*SST|" (°C km"^-1*")"))
```

On a uniform east–west ramp, you should see **non-missing, finite** gradient values (mostly driven by the x-direction).

---

## Sanity checks

```{r sanity}
flat <- sst * 0 + 20
g_flat <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(flat)
g_ramp <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(sst)
mean_flat <- terra::global(g_flat, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
mean_ramp <- terra::global(g_ramp, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
stopifnot(is.finite(mean_flat), is.finite(mean_ramp))
stopifnot(mean_ramp > mean_flat, mean_ramp > 0)
c(flat_mean = mean_flat, ramp_mean = mean_ramp)
```

- **Flat SST** → lower mean |∇SST| than a ramp (edges can be noisy with `pad = TRUE`).  
- **Smooth ramp** → higher mean |∇SST|.  
- If both fail, fix units or stencils before touching real data.

---

## Common confusions (quick table)

| You might think… | Actually… |
|------------------|-----------|
| “Gradient = SST change over days” | That is a **time** derivative; here we difference **across cells** on one day |
| “Kelvin vs Celsius breaks gradients” | **Differences** are the same size; still keep **one convention** for reporting SST |
| “Coastal |∇SST| = offshore fronts” | Coastal magnitudes often reflect **shore structure**, not open-ocean mesoscale fronts |
| “0.083° sees all fronts” | Mesoscale fronts are **partially** resolved; filaments are not |

---

## Paste-ready Methods sentence

> For each calendar day, |∇SST| (°C km⁻¹) was computed on the native SST grid using centred finite differences; cell sizes were converted to kilometres with 111.32 km per degree of latitude and cosine-adjusted longitude spacing. Gradient magnitude was the Euclidean norm of the horizontal partial derivatives.

More detail: [`methods.md`](methods.md).

---

## Next step (conceptual)

When you link to tracking data: **extract** |∇SST| at fix coordinates, then **aggregate** to your model time step (e.g. daily mean). Downloading daily NetCDF from Copernicus is a separate workflow—start from a single SST layer you already trust.
